text.p: Following are some of the leading stories in the Swedish papers this morning. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- A new big bank with a strong focus on retail clients will be formed through the proposed merger of Swedbank and Foreningsbanken that will be unveiled on Tuesday. Together the banks will hold about a quarter of the nation's deposit and loan market. It will also mean the closure of many branches across the country.

- In December 1996 the periscope of a mini-submarine was seen at Vaxholm in Stockholm's archipelago. The newspaper said it was informed by sources that the incident was one of several being investigated.

- Swedish bank Handelsbanken secures its purchase of mortgage lender Stadshypotek with over 98 percent of shares. But it is now speculated that Handelsbanken will sell off sections of Stadshypotek to the highest bidder. This would include the bank's property section.
- Snow boarding is three times more risky than skiing according to a medical study at Tarnaby/Hemavan between 1989 and 1996.

- A merger between Swedbank and Foreningsbanken, expected to be announced on Tuesday, would create Sweden's second largest bank after the newly merged Handelsbanken and Stadshypotek. Combined the two banks have about 14,000 staff and assets of 657 billion crowns compared to Handelsbanken/Stadshypotek's combined balance of 870 billion crowns.

- Swedish telecoms company Telia, Kinnevik's Modern Times Group (MTG) and Sweden's largest commercial television station TV4 are working together for a common standard on digital TV. The new technology will give more channels at lower cost and also gives links to the Internet.

- Trading in shares of Swedbank and Foreningsbanken was stopped on Monday after the banks announced discussions are underway regarding a merger. It is expected that Swedbank, known as Sparbanken in Sweden, will today make public a bid worth about 11.5 billion crowns on Foreningsbanken. The smaller bank's main owner, the farmers' cooperative LRF, is reportedly receptive to the Swedbank offer. LRF owns about 20 percent of share capital.

- Scandinavian airline SAS, facing sharply increased competition on domestic markets, on Monday announced a 31 percent drop in pre-tax profit to 1.82 billion crowns. Chief executive Jan Stenberg said competition was seen intensifying this year.

- Computer Sciences Corp of the U.S. hopes to put Gothenburg on the world map as a centre of information technology for the automobile and truck industry. This development is conditional on AB Volvo selecting CSC as its partner for a planned Information Technology joint venture.

- Trading was stopped on Monday in shares of building firm NCC and Siab and Siab's main owner Lundbergs. None of the firms would comment on the reason but it was speculated that there would be a merger of the building operations of Siab and NCC which is Sweden's second largest construction firm.
